full_judgment:
Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury J : On an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 filed by one Nazim Ahmed, a third-party, a Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the orders dated 7-2-2013 passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 5296 of 2012, 5297 of 2012, 5688 of 2012, 5295 of 2012, 5293 of 2012, 5691 of 2012, 5690 of 2012, 5292 of 2012, 5294 of 2012, 5689 of 2012 and 5692 of 2012 arising out of Ramna Model Police Station Case Nos. 08 dated 4-10-2012, 09 dated 4-10-2012, 10 dated 4-10-2012, 11 dated 4-10-2012, 12 dated 4-10-2012, 13 dated 4-10-2012, 14 dated 4-10-2012, 15 dated 4-10-2012, 16 dated 4-10-2012, 17 dated 4-10-2012 and 18 dated 4-10-2012 under sections 406/409/420/109 of the Penal Code, 1860 read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Ad, 1947 and sections 12 and 4(2) of the Money Laundering Act, 2012 should not be declared to have been based on improper, legally untenable and erroneous consideration and why the same should not, hence, be set-aside with immediate effect and why the promised amount should not be confiscated in any event and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. However, the accused-opposite-party No. 4 Jesmin Islam was granted bail by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge of Dhaka in 11(eleven) Criminal Miscellaneous Cases, namely, 5296 of 2012, 5297 of 2012, 5688 of 2012, 5295 of 2012, 5293 of 2012, 5691 of 2012, 5690 of 2012, 5292 of 2012, 5294 Of 2012, 5689 of 2012 and 5692 of 2012 by his orders dated 7-02-2013 on the condition that she would refund the loan amount (defrauded amount according to the prosecution) to the bank. The granting of bail to the accused-opposite-party No. 4 was reported both in the electronic and print media. Having come to know thereabout, the petitioner Nazim Ahmed came up with an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure with a view to challenging the orders of bail dated 7-2-2013. At the instance. of this third-party Nazim Ahmed, the High Court Division issued the Rule on 11-2-2013. But during the pendency of the Rule, the learned Public Prosecutor filed separate applications before the learned Metropolitan Sessions judge of Dhaka for cancellation of bail granted to the accused-opposite-party No. 4 on 7-2-2013 in all the 11 (eleven) cases on 14-2-2013. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge heard the matter of cancellation on 17-2-2013 and cancelled the bail of the accused-opposite-party No. 4 and directed her to appear before the Court of first instance within the next three days. In obedience to the orders passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge on 17-2-2013, the accused-opposite-party No. 4 surrendered before the Metropolitan Magistracy on 19-2-2013 with a prayer for bail and she was sent to jail-custody after rejection of her prayer for bail and she has been in jail-custody since the. However, the High Court Division passed two orders dated 20-2-2013 and 5-3-2013 in this proceeding. As against those two orders, the accused-opposite-party No. 4 moved the Appellate Division in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 171 of 2013 and 179 of 2013 respectively. The Appellate Division by its order dated 2nd May, 2013 directed this Bench to dispose of the Rule within 4 (four) weeks from date. In accordance with the order dated 2nd May, 2013 of the Appellate Division, this Bench has taken up the Rule for hearing. 

 4. Mr. Md. Eunus Ali Akand, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the accused-opposite-party No. 4 is the Chairperson of Hall-Mark Group Ltd. and Hall-Mark scam is one of the worst in the banking sector of the country and the Sheraton Branch of Sonali Bank Ltd. was defrauded of millions of Taka by the accused-opposite-party No. 4 and her husband and others in connivance with some officials of Sonali Bank Ltd. on the basis of certain spurious documents and as a conscious citizen of the country, the petitioner, though a third-party, came up with the application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure challenging the orders of bail granted to her on 7-2-2013 in all the 11 (eleven) cases. 

 6. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the State-opposite-party No. 1, contends that although the petitioner is admittedly a third-party, yet the fact remains that out of his genuine concern for the failing banking sector of the country, he moved the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule and if bail is granted to the accused-opposite-party No. 4 on the basis of the application for bail filed by her in this proceeding, she may flee the country jeopardizing the investigations of the cases. 

 9. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud also contends that admittedly the investigations of the cases are in progress and there is no chance of ascendance of the accused-opposite-party No. 4, if she is granted bail by the High Court Division and to prove her bonafide conduct, she surrendered before the Court of first instance at the earliest in obedience to the orders of cancellation of bail passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka. 

 12. Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan also submits that the investigations of the cases filed against the accused-opposite-party No. 4 and others are progressing well and if the accused-opposite-party No. 4 is enlarged on bail by this Court, she may flee the country and the investigations of the cases may be hampered thereby. 

 14. Indisputably, the accused-opposite-party No. 4 was granted bail by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge by his orders dated 07-2-2013 in all 11 (eleven) Criminal Miscellaneous Cases, namely, 5296 of 2012, 5297 of 2012, 5688 of 2012, 5295 of 2012, 5293 of 2012, 5691 of 2012, 5690 of 2012, 5292 of 2012, 5294 of 2012, 5689 of 2012 and 5692 of 2012. It is also admitted that the petitioner is a third-party and being a third-party, he invoked the extra-ordinary jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule on 11-2-2013. It transpires that on coming to know about the Rule-issuing order dated 11-2-2013, the learned Public Prosecutor prayed for cancellation of bail of the accused-opposite-party No. 4 before the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka by filing 11 (eleven) Criminal Miscellaneous Cases afresh, that is to say, Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 1290 of 2013, 1291 of 2013, 1292 of 2013, 1293 of 2013, 1294 of 2013, 1295 of 2013, 1296 of 2013, 1297 of 2013, 1298 of 2013, 1299 of 2013 and 1300 of 2013. Anyway, the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge thought it fit to cancel the bail of the accused-opposite-party No. 4 and accordingly he cancelled her bail by his orders dated 17-2-2013 passed in all the 11 (eleven) Criminal Miscellaneous Cases. Undeniably, at the time of cancellation of bail of the accused-opposite-party No. 4 on 17-2-2013, the Rule issued by the High Court Division was pending for adjudication. In all fairness and in deference to the High Court Division, the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge ought to have washed his hands of the matter and waited for the decision of the High Court Division with regard to cancellation of bail of the accused-opposite-party No. 4. But unfortunately instead of so doing, he himself cancelled her bail during the pendency of the Rule. However, the cancellation of bail of the accused-opposite-party No. 4 by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka is a 'fait accompli'. 

 15. With the cancellation of bail of the accused-opposite-party No. 4 by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, the Rule issued by the High Court Division has become infructuous for all practical purposes. As to the question of freezing of the assets of Hall-Mark Group Ltd., suffice it to say that it is the job of the Investigating Agency (Anti-Corruption Commission) which can be done by taking necessary orders to that effect from the Court concerned as and when required. It is an admitted fact that all the cases filed against the accused-opposite-party No. 4 and others are still under investigation. Needless to say, the steps to be taken for tracing and freezing of the assets of Hall-Mark Group Ltd., at the investigation stage of the cases, rest with the Investigating Agency, that is to say, the Anti-Corruption Commission. At this stage, the High Court Division has nothing to do therewith in a proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Given this land-scape, we feel inclined to hold that the component of the Rule-issuing order about the confiscation of the assets of Hall-Mark Group Ltd. is fully and wholly unnecessary. 

 16. As the Rule has become necessarily infructuous with the cancellation of bail of the accused-opposite-party No. 4 by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka, there is nothing left for us for adjudication; albeit a bail application has been filed on behalf of the accused-opposite-party No. 4 before us. As the Rule has become necessarily infructuous, we refrain from making any observation as to the competency of the Rule issued at the instance of an admitted third-party. This question of competency of a Rule issued at the instance of a third-party can be gone into in an appropriate case in future. 

 17. As to the bail application of the accused-opposite-party No. 4 filed before us, we would like to observe that it is an indisputable fact that the accused-opposite-party No. 4 did not challenge the cancellation of her bail by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka by filing Criminal Revisions before the High Court Division under section 435 read with section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In our view, instead of filing the instant application for bail, she ought to have challenged the cancellation of her bail before the High Court Division in its Criminal Revisional Jurisdiction. The present application for bail of the accused-opposite-party No. 4, as we see it, is misconceived when the Rule itself has become infructuous. Accordingly, the application is rejected.
